## blender-mcp
Blender MCP drives a live Blender instance. execute_blender_code runs
arbitrary Python there, so scripts must not assume anything about the user's Blender.

Before writing code, call get_addon_status() to read `blender_version` and get_scene_info() to
see what already exists.

When writing code:
- Look shader nodes up by type, never by name. Node names are localized on a non-English Blender
  UI, so `nodes["Principled BSDF"]` returns None there; use
  `next(n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED")` instead.
- Never hardcode enum identifiers; they change between Blender versions. Read the valid values
  first, e.g.
  `[i.identifier for i in scene.render.image_settings.bl_rna.properties["file_format"].enum_items]`.
- `scene.render.engine` is the exception: it is a dynamic enum and RNA under-reports it, because
  engines registered by add-ons are not RNA enum items. Read the current value, which is always
  valid, and if you must switch engines assign inside `try/except TypeError`; the error lists
  every accepted identifier.
- With `use_nodes` enabled (the default for new materials), set colors on the shader node inputs.
  `material.diffuse_color` only drives viewport display and does not affect the render.

After changing anything, call get_viewport_screenshot() to confirm the result looks right and
get_scene_info() to confirm the objects exist.

Prefer real assets over scripted geometry unless a simple primitive is asked for. Call an
integration's get_*_status tool before using it. Sources:
- Poly Haven: HDRIs for lighting, textures, generic models.
- Sketchfab: realistic and specific real-world models.
- Poly Pizza: stylised low-poly assets. Credit the creator of CC-BY models.
- Hyper3D Rodin, Hunyuan3D, Tripo: generate one custom object at a time. Never generate a
  whole scene, the ground, or parts to assemble; duplicate earlier results instead.
If get_addon_status lists premium_generators, follow the guidance it returns on when to
generate. After importing, check world_bounding_box and f… [truncated]

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

decisions.decision: Architecture: K districts, each a separate ACL9SiteMap actor that runs the UNCHANGED generator (CL9SiteLayout::Generate) on its own sub-seed, module count and world transform. Add FCL9SiteDistrict {Offset (cm from the truck pad), Yaw in {0,90,180,270}, ModuleCount (base), Zones (empty = use the site Zones)} and TArray<FCL9SiteDistrict> Districts on UCL9SiteDef. When Districts is empty, the current single-site path runs byte-identical, so henhouse, farm and pigfarm do not change.
decisions.rationale: There are few consumers, and I verified each one: GameMode::SpawnNight (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646), GameState Rebuild/Clear (CL9GameState.cpp:401,405) and Cheats (CL9Cheats.cpp:46,73). Each turns into a loop. With one actor per district, ISM components are per district for free (CL9SiteMap.cpp:400-426, 656-683). That bounds the per-tile instance scan in Recast's nav gather (verified at InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167) and the quadratic PlaceProps warning loop (CL9SiteMap.cpp:759-783) to farm scale times K. The 200-module behaviour proven by CL9.Map.LargeSite stays valid, and the 128 cap is never approached.
decisions.rejected: Generator lens: multi-root growth in one grid. It needs changes to the placement core (owner mask in Fits, trunk phase, MainCount from the budget at cpp:540, per-district Specials at cpp:554-572, open-yard rules in BuildSegments). Nobody has measured it at N >= 1000. It would still need district-keyed ISM components to fix the nav gather. It is strictly more code and risk than looping 5 consumers. Also rejected: a 'stitch K layouts into one' variant, which needs the same rotation work plus a trunk generator.

decisions.decision: Grid cap row: keep the cap at 128 and do not touch it. The largest district at day 10 is 230 x 1.25 = 288 modules, which gives Span = ceil(sqrt(1728))*2 = 84 cells.
decisions.rationale: Under the district design no layout comes near 128. The generator lens is right that raising the cap would be harmless, but nothing needs it, so it is not done.
decisions.rejected: Raising the cap to 256 or deriving it from the budget (only needed for the single-grid design).

decisions.decision: Generation row: every machine generates K layouts from sub-seeds derived from the one replicated seed: SubSeed_i = HashCombine(Seed, i), with 0 remapped to 1, because Seed 0 builds nothing (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:842). Log LayoutHash and build ms per district. Add a scoped per-phase timer to ACL9SiteMap::Build (Generate / segments / props+lamps / register). Keep the synchronous build. The fallback, if the measured build hitch is over the budget the user sets (see unresolved), is to build one district per frame during the lobby.
decisions.rationale: Only one seed is replicated (CL9GameState.cpp:382-407). Sub-seeds keep determinism with no new replication. The build runs at lobby entry, not at night start (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271, 765-773). The panel verified this, which corrects the draft.
decisions.rejected: Async or streamed generation before anyone has measured a single-frame build.

decisions.decision: District rotation: support Yaw in multiples of 90 degrees by spawning each district actor with its yaw. Change SiteToWorld to GetActorTransform().TransformPosition (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242). Spawn the flap with the actor's rotation and pass it the world-rotated Outward (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465-468). Nothing else needs to change: all ISM instances are local (AddInstance bWorldSpace=false at CL9SiteMap.cpp:504, 549, 567, 786), components and lamps are attached to the root (:422, :679, :802), and night spawns use random yaw, with jars at a zero rotator.
decisions.rationale: Without yaw every gate faces west (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:889, 906-908). Districts would then stack in one N-S column, the yard distances L reach 400-600 m, and 1,000 modules cannot fit the 600 s walk budget. Rotation lets the districts sit as a cross around the truck.
decisions.rejected: A whole-layout rotation pass inside the generator (generator lens). Actor yaw does the same thing with two small edits.

decisions.decision: District count, size and placement: 5 districts on fixed slots in the stage JSON, with the seed filling only their contents. Initial slots: East (yaw 0) and West (yaw 180) at about 230 base modules each with gates at L of about 10-30 m; North and South (yaw 90/270) at about 190 each with L of about 210 m; one far district at about 160 with L of about 300 m. That sums to about 1,000 base modules (user decision 1). Size rule per district, from stage.md:58-59 with NightLength 600 and MainPathShare 0.30: 1.59*N_i + 0.444*L_i <= 440 (one-way yard distance L in metres at 4.5 m/s). Slots may not overlap as rotated day-10 span rectangles. Final offsets are set after the footprint measurement.
decisions.rationale: The project applies the night formula at base count; farm is 480 s at base 200 and gets no day-10 correction, because NightLengthCurve is flat. Every district can then be raided to its deep zone and back within one night, while all five clearly cannot (user decisions 2 and 3). Near districts are larger and far ones smaller and denser. Fixed slots satisfy both the nav lens (deterministic bounds) and the play lens (walk budget).
decisions.rejected: Equal 5 x 200 districts: N/S and far districts would break the 600 s budget. The play lens example also misstated that its sizes hold on day 10 (230 at L=10 gives 1.99*230 > 440). The project convention is base count, so the sizes are kept but applied at base.

decisions.decision: Truck and yard: one truck pad, the existing ACL9TruckPad, at the yard centre. It anchors every district actor (pad + rotated offset). The yard is the level's bare floor plane, scaled by setup_stage.py to the union of rotated day-10 district rectangles plus MARGIN. There are no generated yard modules, no yard content and no yard monsters in the first cut.
decisions.rationale: This is the smallest change. setup_stage already scales the Floor/Ground actors (setup_stage.py:169-196). A generated yard would add fenced paddocks (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1072-1113) or a large Grid instance count for nothing. Monsters are leashed to HomeRange (CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132, 1240-1241), so an empty yard costs no AI.
decisions.rejected: Yards made of yard_open modules, open-yard segment rules and a new road row in the 'henhouse' theme, which would change the henhouse/farm/pigfarm pools.

decisions.decision: Entrances and exits: each district keeps the generator's own yard_gate (Start, facing the truck after yaw) and its own single flapIn at its deepest dead end. Record in docs/decisions.md that module.md decision 3 ('one entrance, one flap') applies per district building, and that the truck docks at the stage pad rather than at each gate.
decisions.rationale: User decision 3 makes districts separate building clusters, and each one has to be enterable. One entrance plus one fire exit per building matches the Lethal-interior analogue that module.md:193-195 cites. It costs no code, because the generator already does it per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908, 969), and the four one-flap test assertions stay valid per layout.
decisions.rejected: One entrance and one flap for the whole stage. Only the single-grid design can express that, and it makes the far districts reachable only through the near ones.

decisions.decision: Depth zones: depth is evaluated per district (per-layout hop normalisation, CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217, unchanged). Districts differ through an optional per-district Zones override (reusing FCL9SiteZone); an empty override uses the site Zones. Far districts get heavier rows (more pig, raccoon and meat). ValueRate stays 1.0.
decisions.rationale: This answers the generator lens objection that per-district normalisation makes every district identical. It reuses the existing struct and the existing SpawnNight zone loop (CL9GameMode.cpp:600-613), called once per district.
decisions.rejected: Global hop depth across one grid (needs the single grid). Also a new per-district danger tier or DepthBias column, which is extra data on top of the Zones override.

decisions.decision: Nav row: keep dynamic runtime navmesh with the default TileSizeUU 1000 and no invokers. setup_stage.py sizes ONE NavMeshBoundsVolume to the union of district rectangles plus margin, so the yard is navmeshed and the truck-to-gate paths can be checked. On the host, StartNight defers itself with a retry timer while the navigation build is in progress, and logs the wait. This needs no UI.
decisions.rationale: The map and its nav build happen in the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271, 765-773). Nothing currently waits for nav before night start, and that gap is the real failure mode. With per-district ISM components, empty yard tiles scan no instances. Invokers either violate decision 4 or move the build into the night, and they are a global setting that would also change the other stages. The current code path stays: one box, just bigger.
decisions.rejected: Navigation invokers (violate decision 4 or move the build into the night). Per-slot volumes with no yard navmesh: kept as the fallback if the union build is too slow, because the union box is the existing path and makes the yard testable. A larger tile size up front: only after measurement.

decisions.decision: Rendering row: no HLOD and no district distance or visibility culling system in the first cut. Per-district actors give per-district components, so frustum and occlusion culling works per district. Log the lamp count and the flicker-lamp count next to the existing build log lines (CL9SiteMap.cpp:630-635). The fallback, only if yard-view GPU Lights/VolumetricFog is over budget, is MaxDrawDistance on lamps plus skipping TickFlicker beyond it (CL9SiteMap.cpp:286-303, 789-818). LampDensity stays the total-count lever.
decisions.rationale: performance.md:22/94 forbid optimisation before measurement. Collision must stay on every district on the server because far monsters walk against WorldStatic (decision 4). Ray tracing is already distance-culled at 300 m.
decisions.rejected: Per-district show/hide (it does not remove physics or nav cost, and toggling re-creates instance bodies). HLOD.

decisions.decision: Host monster cost under decision 4: AI, senses and movement always run. The monster MeshComponent sets VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered in C++ (only the player overrides it today, at CL9Character.cpp:147). No think-rate LOD and no distance sleep.
decisions.rationale: No CL9 C++ uses montages or notifies, and the only bone read is the cosmetic hit puff (CL9Monster.cpp:405). Movement is code-driven (AddActorWorldOffset), so skipping unseen poses does not change behaviour. OnlyTickMontages is chosen over OnlyTickPose in case a Blueprint uses montage notifies. Skeletal animation is the largest per-monster item (performance.md:118-119).
decisions.rejected: Think-rate LOD by distance. It can be read as distance throttling against decision 4, so if the measurement fails the fallback is lowering counts, not throttling.

decisions.decision: Population row and monster total: per district, roughly one Lethal interior. Base zone sums are about 9 (East/West), 11 (North/South) and 13 (far), about 53 in total. Through the existing MonsterCountCurve (0.6 on day 1, 1.0 on day 5, 1.5 on day 10, progression.md:29) that gives about 32 monsters on day 1, about 53 on day 5 and about 80 on day 10. Per district on day 10 that is about 13-20, against Titan's indoor 18 power at 1-3 power per enemy (lethal-map.md:204, lethal-monsters.md:595-629). Items keep the farm's per-module density (about 0.35 per module at base, farm.json:26-28), with far overrides weighted toward meat. Night spawning stays synchronous until it is measured; the fallback is time-sliced spawning.
decisions.rationale: This is a compromise between the nav-ai lens (about 45 / 80) and the play lens (35-40 / 90-100). It uses only existing data (Zones x day curve), with no new power system. It is about one third of a blind 5x of the farm (125 / 300), which user decision 4 rules out.
decisions.rejected: A Lethal-style power budget and spawn ramp (new code). 5x the farm density.

decisions.decision: Night row: NightLength 600, DarkBase 450, DarkMin 300 (the farm's 360/240 scaled by 600/480). One night, no multi-trip.
decisions.rationale: User decision 2. It keeps DarkMin <= DarkBase <= NightLength (stage.md:53), and the district size rule keeps every district within one night.
decisions.rejected: 30-50 min nights (from the original spec estimate).

decisions.decision: Walk-time row: do not add vehicles or shortcuts. Walk time is bounded by the per-district size rule plus jars. It is validated by a scripted walk truck -> gate -> deepest point -> nearest jar -> truck for each district.
decisions.rationale: The formula comes from only two data points (stage.md:58-59), so it must be checked by measurement.
decisions.rejected: Moving the truck, or several trips per night.

decisions.decision: Return jars row: SpecialCopies (the existing site column, inherited as 4 from farm) applies per district, because each layout reads Params.SpecialCopies. That gives about 4 delivery rooms per district, about 20 in all. The jar dedupe set in SpawnNight resets per district, since module indices are per layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:625-633).
decisions.rationale: This needs no new data and it already works per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:529, 556).
decisions.rejected: Reinterpreting SpecialCopies as per-district in a single grid.

decisions.decision: Relevancy: keep the default NetCullDistance (150 m) and do not make monsters always relevant. Measure the client hitch when crossing between districts in 2-client PIE.
decisions.rationale: Client cost stays bounded. Today no CL9 actor overrides it (CL9ActorBase.cpp:9).
decisions.rejected: Raising the cull distance up front.

decisions.decision: QA and tests: (1) CL9.Map.Districts: 30 seeds at each slot's day-10 module count (max 288); assert build, IsConnected, no overlap, one flap, at least 2 delivery rooms and at least 90% of budget; log ms and the occupied bounding box. (2) Slot test on the giant row: rotated day-10 rectangles do not overlap and every L_i satisfies the size rule. (3) Existing LargeSite and DepthBand stay unchanged as the guard that Districts-empty output is identical. (4) qa_farm_stage_pie.py: take the nav window from the union bounds instead of the hard-coded -10..400 / +-200 m (qa_farm_stage_pie.py:141-143); record nav-done seconds, monster state counts per sample, ever-moved, and the build-log counts (lamps included). (5) perf_probe spots: lobby-day yard, night yard facing the districts, and the deepest district interior, after first taking a Lvl_Farm baseline at equivalent spots.
decisions.rationale: The current script cannot gate a 1 km stage (render lens, verified line references). LargeSite only covers 200 modules.
decisions.rejected: Running layout tests at 1,000 modules in one layout, which tests a code path this design never runs.

unresolved.question: The CL9 game-thread budget of 4 ms or less (performance.md:18, with 4 players and the maximum monster spawn) already fails on henhouse: 4.9 ms with 7 monsters. With about 80 always-active monsters on day 10, should 4 ms stay a hard acceptance gate for this stage, or should the gate be the frame target only (avg 16.7 ms / p95 25 ms), with game-thread ms reported?
options: Keep 4 ms as a hard gate (monster counts drop until it passes)
Gate on avg 16.7 / p95 25 ms only; report the CL9 game-thread ms and record a new budget in decisions.md
Set a new game-thread number for the giant stage
unresolved.why_user_only: It is the user's performance budget. performance.md:17 says to either fix or re-budget, and the gate decides how many monsters decision 4 can afford.

unresolved.question: What hitch is acceptable for (a) building the K-district site at lobby entry and on client join, done synchronously on every machine, and (b) spawning about 80 monsters at night start (measured at 98 ms per 10)? performance.md defines no hitch budget for either.
options: Accept any one-off transition hitch behind the dawn/lobby fade and just record it
A fixed ceiling per transition (user gives the ms number); over it, build one district per frame and time-slice spawns
Always time-slice both regardless of measurement
unresolved.why_user_only: No existing document sets the number. It is a feel and quality bar that only the user can set, and it decides whether the one-district-per-frame and time-sliced spawn fallbacks are built.

measure_first: Lvl_Farm perf_probe baseline at equivalent spots (lobby-day at the truck, night yard, night deep interior). Without it the +1 ms regression rule (performance.md:17) has nothing to compare against. No fallback: this must run before any giant-stage frame numbers.

District footprint: the occupied bounding box (not the span) over 30 seeds at 160-290 modules, logged by CL9.Map.Districts. If the building covers much less than the span, pull the N/S/far slots closer (smaller L, sizes can rise toward the rule). Fallback: place slots by full rotated day-10 span rectangles, which is safe and gives larger L, and shrink the far districts per the size rule.

Generation fill and time at each slot's day-10 count (max 288, Span 84) over 30 seeds. Fallback if fill is under 90% or a seed fails: move modules from that slot to the near slots, keeping the total at about 1,000.

Positions of the food truck, kitchen and counter actors relative to the truck pad in the source level. Fallback if the West arm (yaw 180) collides: move the West gate outward and cut its N per the size rule, or move that budget to the far slot.

Nav: seconds from SetSiteMap until the navigation build finishes, tile count and navmesh memory, for the union bounds box. Fallback if it takes longer than about 100 s (the farm's under 20 s x 5 districts, the linear expectation): per-slot NavMeshBoundsVolumes with no yard navmesh, then compare TileSizeUU 1000 and 2000, including the cart-push rebuild cost.

Before changing the anim tick option: check the five monster ABPs/BPs for montage or notify-driven gameplay. Fallback if one exists: OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered already keeps montages; if pose-driven gameplay exists, keep AlwaysTick for that species only.

Host frame with the day-10 monster count (about 80) all forced awake and wandering, after the anim change. perf_probe avg/p95/GPU and stat dumpframe at the three spots, with 1 client. Fallback if over budget: lower the per-district zone counts (data only). Never sleep or throttle by distance (decision 4).

Per-phase site build ms on host and client for K=5, including CreateAllInstanceBodies, and process memory before and after (16 GB machine, 2-client PIE). Fallback: register one district per frame during the lobby, if it exceeds the hitch budget the user sets.
Lamp and flicker-lamp counts plus stat gpu Lights/VolumetricFog in the yard view. Fallback: lamp MaxDrawDistance and skip TickFlicker beyond it.
Night-start spawn spike at day-10 counts. Fallback: time-sliced spawning (a few monsters per frame), if it exceeds the user's hitch budget.

Scripted walk truck -> gate -> deepest point -> nearest jar -> truck for each district at base size, against 600 s. Fallback: adjust that slot's ModuleCount or L. MainPathShare 0.30 is the inherited lever if every district runs long.

2-client PIE: client LayoutHash for each district equals the host's, plus stat dumphitches while a client crosses the yard between districts. Fallback only if a hitch appears: per-species NetCullDistance tuning or anim-instance pooling.
acceptance: Henhouse, farm and pigfarm are unchanged: the existing CL9.Map.LargeSite and CL9.Map.DepthBand pass with identical logged hashes (seed 873, CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:541-658), and the Districts-empty path is byte-identical (giant-stage.md out-of-scope).

CL9.Map.Districts: for every slot, 30 seeds at that slot's day-10 count (base x 1.25, progression.md:35) all build, IsConnected holds, no overlap, exactly 1 flap, at least 2 delivery rooms, at least 90% of the ground budget, and generation ms is logged per layout (giant-stage.md acceptance 1).

Slot test: the giant row's district base ModuleCounts sum to 1,000 +- 5% (user decision 1). No two rotated day-10 span rectangles overlap. Every district satisfies 1.59*N_i + 0.444*L_i <= 440 (stage.md:58-59 with NightLength 600, MainPathShare 0.30, 4.5 m/s).
Determinism: in 2-client PIE every client logs the same LayoutHash as the host for each of the 5 districts (user decision 5).

Nav: StartNight does not start while the host navigation build is in progress. All spawned monsters project onto the navmesh within a 100-unit extent. A nav path exists from the truck pad to every district gate. Nav-done seconds are recorded (target at most about 100 s, else the per-slot-volume fallback).

Population: logged night totals are about 32 monsters on day 1 and about 80 on day 10 (base zone sum about 53 x MonsterCountCurve 0.6 / 1.5, progression.md:29). In a forced-awake pass every monster is still spawned and ticking AI at +90 s with no distance despawn (user decision 4).

Frame: perf_probe in 1-client editor PIE at the lobby-day yard, night yard and deepest-district interior with the day-10 monster count: avg <= 16.7 ms and p95 <= 25 ms (performance.md:16), GPU <= 10 ms (performance.md:19). CL9 game-thread ms is reported against performance.md:18 as the user decides.

Night: NightLength 600 s, DarkBase 450, DarkMin 300 on the giant row. A scripted walk truck -> gate -> deepest point -> nearest jar -> truck completes within 600 s for every district at base size (giant-stage.md acceptance 3, user decision 2).
Build logs show, per district, modules, instances, components, props, lamps, flicker lamps and per-phase build ms, and qa JSON records them.

work_split.work: Add the FCL9SiteDistrict struct and the Districts array to UCL9SiteDef. In ACL9SiteMap: a district index and transform; Build takes the district's ModuleCount (instead of BaseModuleCount x SiteSize at CL9SiteMap.cpp:349-350, keeping the day multiplier) and the sub-seed (nonzero); SiteToWorld through the actor transform; flap spawn rotation and world Outward; FindAll/Rebuild/Clear loops (keep Find for the single path); per-district LayoutHash log; per-phase timer; lamp and flicker counts in the log. GameState RebuildSiteMap and the cheat LayEditorSiteMap loop over the districts. Tests: CL9.Map.Districts plus the slot test.

setup_stage.py: read a 'districts' list from the stage JSON into the row, and compute the union of rotated day-10 grid rectangles (reuse grid_extent per district) for Floor/Ground and the single NavMeshBoundsVolume. Create stages\giant.json (inherit farm columns, 5 slots, night 600/450/300) and a new level copied as for farm (delete the saved RecastNavMesh). qa_farm_stage_pie.py: nav window from union bounds, nav-done time, monster state counts and ever-moved, build-log counts, nav path truck->each gate, 100-unit projection.

SpawnNightPopulation loops over every district SiteMap: per-district point lists, the district Zones override or the site Zones, a jar dedupe set reset per district. StartNight defers with a retry timer while the host navigation build is in progress. Monster mesh VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered, after the ABP check.

Fix the slot offsets and ModuleCounts by the size rule and the measured footprint. Fill the per-district zone overrides: base sums of about 9/9/11/11/13 monsters (about 53), items at farm per-module density, far districts weighted toward pig, raccoon and meat. Night 600/450/300. ValueRate stays 1.0.

Record the decisions in decisions.md: districts as K SiteMap actors; module.md decision 3 applies per district; monster total and its Lethal comparison; no invokers; anim tick option. Update stage.md (Districts column, size rule), map.md (giant level measurements), site.md (district table), performance.md (Lvl_Farm baseline and giant numbers), and giant-stage.md acceptance with the final numbers.

None in the first cut. The existing henhouse theme modules, pieces and gate campfire are reused, and no new rows are added to the 'henhouse' theme. The outdoor backdrop (docs/goal/outdoor-backdrop.md) must be placed outside the district union bounds.
None in the first cut. Night start defers silently with a log, and districts are told apart only by the gate campfire and their visible size and distance. Revisit if playtests show a blind choice.

weak_points: The size rule rests on stage.md's two-point fit (night = 160 + 5.3 x spine) and an unmeasured 4.5 m/s yard speed. Carrying slowdown f(weight) is undecided (economy.md:125-126) and carts move at 2.97 m/s, so real round trips for the far districts may exceed 600 s until the walk test is done.

Reading module.md decision 3 as 'per district' gives 5 gates (each with a campfire) and 5 one-way flaps. If the user meant one exit per stage, CarveEmergencyExit would need a per-district off switch. This interpretation is recorded in decisions.md rather than asked.

The cross layout depends on actor-yaw correctness. Any CL9 code that assumes a zero-rotation site frame beyond SiteToWorld and the flap (for example Python QA math, outdoor-backdrop placement, or debug drawing) will place things wrongly for the N/S/West districts. Only the C++ consumers were grepped.

The monster total (about 32 on day 1, about 80 on day 10) is a judgement by Lethal comparison. Per-district density is about a third of the farm's, which may make a raided district feel emptier than the farm. Per-species power mapping was not done.
Per-monster host cost after the anim change is unmeasured. If unrendered monsters still cost about 0.1 ms each, 80 monsters is about 8 ms, and the only allowed lever is lower counts.

One union NavMeshBoundsVolume navmeshes the empty yard. Build time for about 11-13k tiles is extrapolated linearly from the farm's about 2,070 tiles in under 20 s, which was measured from night start, not from the lobby.
setup_stage.py keeps a hand-copied Span formula (setup_stage.py:79), now applied per district with rotation. Any future change to the C++ formula silently desyncs floor and nav bounds.
Blueprint subclasses or ABPs were not inspected for montage notifies or VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption overrides; only C++ was grepped.
Players have no information for choosing a district beyond landmarks. User decision 3's 'choose which district' may become a blind pick until UI or signage is designed.
Item count at farm density per module is about 350 physics items across the stage. Replication and physics cost for them was not analysed beyond the 150 m relevancy default.

decisions.decision: Architecture: K districts, each a separate ACL9SiteMap actor that runs the UNCHANGED generator (CL9SiteLayout::Generate) on its own sub-seed, module count and world transform. Add FCL9SiteDistrict {Offset (cm from the truck pad), Yaw in {0,90,180,270}, ModuleCount (base), Zones (empty = use the site Zones)} and TArray<FCL9SiteDistrict> Districts on UCL9SiteDef. When Districts is empty, the current single-site path runs byte-identical, so henhouse, farm and pigfarm do not change.
decisions.rationale: There are few consumers, and I verified each one: GameMode::SpawnNight (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646), GameState Rebuild/Clear (CL9GameState.cpp:401,405) and Cheats (CL9Cheats.cpp:46,73). Each turns into a loop. With one actor per district, ISM components are per district for free (CL9SiteMap.cpp:400-426, 656-683). That bounds the per-tile instance scan in Recast's nav gather (verified at InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167) and the quadratic PlaceProps warning loop (CL9SiteMap.cpp:759-783) to farm scale times K. The 200-module behaviour proven by CL9.Map.LargeSite stays valid, and the 128 cap is never approached.
decisions.rejected: Generator lens: multi-root growth in one grid. It needs changes to the placement core (owner mask in Fits, trunk phase, MainCount from the budget at cpp:540, per-district Specials at cpp:554-572, open-yard rules in BuildSegments). Nobody has measured it at N >= 1000. It would still need district-keyed ISM components to fix the nav gather. It is strictly more code and risk than looping 5 consumers. Also rejected: a 'stitch K layouts into one' variant, which needs the same rotation work plus a trunk generator.

decisions.decision: Grid cap row: keep the cap at 128 and do not touch it. The largest district at day 10 is 230 x 1.25 = 288 modules, which gives Span = ceil(sqrt(1728))*2 = 84 cells.
decisions.rationale: Under the district design no layout comes near 128. The generator lens is right that raising the cap would be harmless, but nothing needs it, so it is not done.
decisions.rejected: Raising the cap to 256 or deriving it from the budget (only needed for the single-grid design).

decisions.decision: Generation row: every machine generates K layouts from sub-seeds derived from the one replicated seed: SubSeed_i = HashCombine(Seed, i), with 0 remapped to 1, because Seed 0 builds nothing (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:842). Log LayoutHash and build ms per district. Add a scoped per-phase timer to ACL9SiteMap::Build (Generate / segments / props+lamps / register). Keep the synchronous build. The fallback, if the measured build hitch is over the budget the user sets (see unresolved), is to build one district per frame during the lobby.
decisions.rationale: Only one seed is replicated (CL9GameState.cpp:382-407). Sub-seeds keep determinism with no new replication. The build runs at lobby entry, not at night start (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271, 765-773). The panel verified this, which corrects the draft.
decisions.rejected: Async or streamed generation before anyone has measured a single-frame build.

decisions.decision: District rotation: support Yaw in multiples of 90 degrees by spawning each district actor with its yaw. Change SiteToWorld to GetActorTransform().TransformPosition (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242). Spawn the flap with the actor's rotation and pass it the world-rotated Outward (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465-468). Nothing else needs to change: all ISM instances are local (AddInstance bWorldSpace=false at CL9SiteMap.cpp:504, 549, 567, 786), components and lamps are attached to the root (:422, :679, :802), and night spawns use random yaw, with jars at a zero rotator.
decisions.rationale: Without yaw every gate faces west (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:889, 906-908). Districts would then stack in one N-S column, the yard distances L reach 400-600 m, and 1,000 modules cannot fit the 600 s walk budget. Rotation lets the districts sit as a cross around the truck.
decisions.rejected: A whole-layout rotation pass inside the generator (generator lens). Actor yaw does the same thing with two small edits.

decisions.decision: District count, size and placement: 5 districts on fixed slots in the stage JSON, with the seed filling only their contents. Initial slots: East (yaw 0) and West (yaw 180) at about 230 base modules each with gates at L of about 10-30 m; North and South (yaw 90/270) at about 190 each with L of about 210 m; one far district at about 160 with L of about 300 m. That sums to about 1,000 base modules (user decision 1). Size rule per district, from stage.md:58-59 with NightLength 600 and MainPathShare 0.30: 1.59*N_i + 0.444*L_i <= 440 (one-way yard distance L in metres at 4.5 m/s). Slots may not overlap as rotated day-10 span rectangles. Final offsets are set after the footprint measurement.
decisions.rationale: The project applies the night formula at base count; farm is 480 s at base 200 and gets no day-10 correction, because NightLengthCurve is flat. Every district can then be raided to its deep zone and back within one night, while all five clearly cannot (user decisions 2 and 3). Near districts are larger and far ones smaller and denser. Fixed slots satisfy both the nav lens (deterministic bounds) and the play lens (walk budget).
decisions.rejected: Equal 5 x 200 districts: N/S and far districts would break the 600 s budget. The play lens example also misstated that its sizes hold on day 10 (230 at L=10 gives 1.99*230 > 440). The project convention is base count, so the sizes are kept but applied at base.

decisions.decision: Truck and yard: one truck pad, the existing ACL9TruckPad, at the yard centre. It anchors every district actor (pad + rotated offset). The yard is the level's bare floor plane, scaled by setup_stage.py to the union of rotated day-10 district rectangles plus MARGIN. There are no generated yard modules, no yard content and no yard monsters in the first cut.
decisions.rationale: This is the smallest change. setup_stage already scales the Floor/Ground actors (setup_stage.py:169-196). A generated yard would add fenced paddocks (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1072-1113) or a large Grid instance count for nothing. Monsters are leashed to HomeRange (CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132, 1240-1241), so an empty yard costs no AI.
decisions.rejected: Yards made of yard_open modules, open-yard segment rules and a new road row in the 'henhouse' theme, which would change the henhouse/farm/pigfarm pools.

decisions.decision: Entrances and exits: each district keeps the generator's own yard_gate (Start, facing the truck after yaw) and its own single flapIn at its deepest dead end. Record in docs/decisions.md that module.md decision 3 ('one entrance, one flap') applies per district building, and that the truck docks at the stage pad rather than at each gate.
decisions.rationale: User decision 3 makes districts separate building clusters, and each one has to be enterable. One entrance plus one fire exit per building matches the Lethal-interior analogue that module.md:193-195 cites. It costs no code, because the generator already does it per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908, 969), and the four one-flap test assertions stay valid per layout.
decisions.rejected: One entrance and one flap for the whole stage. Only the single-grid design can express that, and it makes the far districts reachable only through the near ones.

decisions.decision: Depth zones: depth is evaluated per district (per-layout hop normalisation, CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217, unchanged). Districts differ through an optional per-district Zones override (reusing FCL9SiteZone); an empty override uses the site Zones. Far districts get heavier rows (more pig, raccoon and meat). ValueRate stays 1.0.
decisions.rationale: This answers the generator lens objection that per-district normalisation makes every district identical. It reuses the existing struct and the existing SpawnNight zone loop (CL9GameMode.cpp:600-613), called once per district.
decisions.rejected: Global hop depth across one grid (needs the single grid). Also a new per-district danger tier or DepthBias column, which is extra data on top of the Zones override.

decisions.decision: Nav row: keep dynamic runtime navmesh with the default TileSizeUU 1000 and no invokers. setup_stage.py sizes ONE NavMeshBoundsVolume to the union of district rectangles plus margin, so the yard is navmeshed and the truck-to-gate paths can be checked. On the host, StartNight defers itself with a retry timer while the navigation build is in progress, and logs the wait. This needs no UI.
decisions.rationale: The map and its nav build happen in the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271, 765-773). Nothing currently waits for nav before night start, and that gap is the real failure mode. With per-district ISM components, empty yard tiles scan no instances. Invokers either violate decision 4 or move the build into the night, and they are a global setting that would also change the other stages. The current code path stays: one box, just bigger.
decisions.rejected: Navigation invokers (violate decision 4 or move the build into the night). Per-slot volumes with no yard navmesh: kept as the fallback if the union build is too slow, because the union box is the existing path and makes the yard testable. A larger tile size up front: only after measurement.

decisions.decision: QA and tests: (1) CL9.Map.Districts: 30 seeds at each slot's day-10 module count (max 288); assert build, IsConnected, no overlap, one flap, at least 2 delivery rooms and at least 90% of budget; log ms and the occupied bounding box. (2) Slot test on the giant row: rotated day-10 rectangles do not overlap and every L_i satisfies the size rule. (3) Existing LargeSite and DepthBand stay unchanged as the guard that Districts-empty output is identical. (4) qa_farm_stage_pie.py: take the nav window from the union bounds instead of the hard-coded -10..400 / +-200 m (qa_farm_stage_pie.py:141-143); record nav-done seconds, monster state counts per sample, ever-moved, and the build-log counts (lamps included). (5) perf_probe spots: lobby-day yard, night yard facing the districts, and the deepest district interior, after first taking a Lvl_Farm baseline at equivalent spots.
decisions.rationale: The current script cannot gate a 1 km stage (render lens, verified line references). LargeSite only covers 200 modules.
decisions.rejected: Running layout tests at 1,000 modules in one layout, which tests a code path this design never runs.

unresolved.question: The CL9 game-thread budget of 4 ms or less (performance.md:18, with 4 players and the maximum monster spawn) already fails on henhouse: 4.9 ms with 7 monsters. With about 80 always-active monsters on day 10, should 4 ms stay a hard acceptance gate for this stage, or should the gate be the frame target only (avg 16.7 ms / p95 25 ms), with game-thread ms reported?
options: Keep 4 ms as a hard gate (monster counts drop until it passes)
Gate on avg 16.7 / p95 25 ms only; report the CL9 game-thread ms and record a new budget in decisions.md
Set a new game-thread number for the giant stage
unresolved.why_user_only: It is the user's performance budget. performance.md:17 says to either fix or re-budget, and the gate decides how many monsters decision 4 can afford.

unresolved.question: What hitch is acceptable for (a) building the K-district site at lobby entry and on client join, done synchronously on every machine, and (b) spawning about 80 monsters at night start (measured at 98 ms per 10)? performance.md defines no hitch budget for either.
options: Accept any one-off transition hitch behind the dawn/lobby fade and just record it
A fixed ceiling per transition (user gives the ms number); over it, build one district per frame and time-slice spawns
Always time-slice both regardless of measurement
unresolved.why_user_only: No existing document sets the number. It is a feel and quality bar that only the user can set, and it decides whether the one-district-per-frame and time-sliced spawn fallbacks are built.

measure_first: Lvl_Farm perf_probe baseline at equivalent spots (lobby-day at the truck, night yard, night deep interior). Without it the +1 ms regression rule (performance.md:17) has nothing to compare against. No fallback: this must run before any giant-stage frame numbers.

District footprint: the occupied bounding box (not the span) over 30 seeds at 160-290 modules, logged by CL9.Map.Districts. If the building covers much less than the span, pull the N/S/far slots closer (smaller L, sizes can rise toward the rule). Fallback: place slots by full rotated day-10 span rectangles, which is safe and gives larger L, and shrink the far districts per the size rule.

Generation fill and time at each slot's day-10 count (max 288, Span 84) over 30 seeds. Fallback if fill is under 90% or a seed fails: move modules from that slot to the near slots, keeping the total at about 1,000.

Positions of the food truck, kitchen and counter actors relative to the truck pad in the source level. Fallback if the West arm (yaw 180) collides: move the West gate outward and cut its N per the size rule, or move that budget to the far slot.

Nav: seconds from SetSiteMap until the navigation build finishes, tile count and navmesh memory, for the union bounds box. Fallback if it takes longer than about 100 s (the farm's under 20 s x 5 districts, the linear expectation): per-slot NavMeshBoundsVolumes with no yard navmesh, then compare TileSizeUU 1000 and 2000, including the cart-push rebuild cost.

Before changing the anim tick option: check the five monster ABPs/BPs for montage or notify-driven gameplay. Fallback if one exists: OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered already keeps montages; if pose-driven gameplay exists, keep AlwaysTick for that species only.

Host frame with the day-10 monster count (about 80) all forced awake and wandering, after the anim change. perf_probe avg/p95/GPU and stat dumpframe at the three spots, with 1 client. Fallback if over budget: lower the per-district zone counts (data only). Never sleep or throttle by distance (decision 4).

Per-phase site build ms on host and client for K=5, including CreateAllInstanceBodies, and process memory before and after (16 GB machine, 2-client PIE). Fallback: register one district per frame during the lobby, if it exceeds the hitch budget the user sets.
Lamp and flicker-lamp counts plus stat gpu Lights/VolumetricFog in the yard view. Fallback: lamp MaxDrawDistance and skip TickFlicker beyond it.
Night-start spawn spike at day-10 counts. Fallback: time-sliced spawning (a few monsters per frame), if it exceeds the user's hitch budget.

Scripted walk truck -> gate -> deepest point -> nearest jar -> truck for each district at base size, against 600 s. Fallback: adjust that slot's ModuleCount or L. MainPathShare 0.30 is the inherited lever if every district runs long.

2-client PIE: client LayoutHash for each district equals the host's, plus stat dumphitches while a client crosses the yard between districts. Fallback only if a hitch appears: per-species NetCullDistance tuning or anim-instance pooling.
acceptance: Henhouse, farm and pigfarm are unchanged: the existing CL9.Map.LargeSite and CL9.Map.DepthBand pass with identical logged hashes (seed 873, CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:541-658), and the Districts-empty path is byte-identical (giant-stage.md out-of-scope).

CL9.Map.Districts: for every slot, 30 seeds at that slot's day-10 count (base x 1.25, progression.md:35) all build, IsConnected holds, no overlap, exactly 1 flap, at least 2 delivery rooms, at least 90% of the ground budget, and generation ms is logged per layout (giant-stage.md acceptance 1).

Slot test: the giant row's district base ModuleCounts sum to 1,000 +- 5% (user decision 1). No two rotated day-10 span rectangles overlap. Every district satisfies 1.59*N_i + 0.444*L_i <= 440 (stage.md:58-59 with NightLength 600, MainPathShare 0.30, 4.5 m/s).
Determinism: in 2-client PIE every client logs the same LayoutHash as the host for each of the 5 districts (user decision 5).

Nav: StartNight does not start while the host navigation build is in progress. All spawned monsters project onto the navmesh within a 100-unit extent. A nav path exists from the truck pad to every district gate. Nav-done seconds are recorded (target at most about 100 s, else the per-slot-volume fallback).

Population: logged night totals are about 32 monsters on day 1 and about 80 on day 10 (base zone sum about 53 x MonsterCountCurve 0.6 / 1.5, progression.md:29). In a forced-awake pass every monster is still spawned and ticking AI at +90 s with no distance despawn (user decision 4).

Frame: perf_probe in 1-client editor PIE at the lobby-day yard, night yard and deepest-district interior with the day-10 monster count: avg <= 16.7 ms and p95 <= 25 ms (performance.md:16), GPU <= 10 ms (performance.md:19). CL9 game-thread ms is reported against performance.md:18 as the user decides.

Night: NightLength 600 s, DarkBase 450, DarkMin 300 on the giant row. A scripted walk truck -> gate -> deepest point -> nearest jar -> truck completes within 600 s for every district at base size (giant-stage.md acceptance 3, user decision 2).
Build logs show, per district, modules, instances, components, props, lamps, flicker lamps and per-phase build ms, and qa JSON records them.

work_split.work: Add the FCL9SiteDistrict struct and the Districts array to UCL9SiteDef. In ACL9SiteMap: a district index and transform; Build takes the district's ModuleCount (instead of BaseModuleCount x SiteSize at CL9SiteMap.cpp:349-350, keeping the day multiplier) and the sub-seed (nonzero); SiteToWorld through the actor transform; flap spawn rotation and world Outward; FindAll/Rebuild/Clear loops (keep Find for the single path); per-district LayoutHash log; per-phase timer; lamp and flicker counts in the log. GameState RebuildSiteMap and the cheat LayEditorSiteMap loop over the districts. Tests: CL9.Map.Districts plus the slot test.

setup_stage.py: read a 'districts' list from the stage JSON into the row, and compute the union of rotated day-10 grid rectangles (reuse grid_extent per district) for Floor/Ground and the single NavMeshBoundsVolume. Create stages\giant.json (inherit farm columns, 5 slots, night 600/450/300) and a new level copied as for farm (delete the saved RecastNavMesh). qa_farm_stage_pie.py: nav window from union bounds, nav-done time, monster state counts and ever-moved, build-log counts, nav path truck->each gate, 100-unit projection.

SpawnNightPopulation loops over every district SiteMap: per-district point lists, the district Zones override or the site Zones, a jar dedupe set reset per district. StartNight defers with a retry timer while the host navigation build is in progress. Monster mesh VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered, after the ABP check.

Fix the slot offsets and ModuleCounts by the size rule and the measured footprint. Fill the per-district zone overrides: base sums of about 9/9/11/11/13 monsters (about 53), items at farm per-module density, far districts weighted toward pig, raccoon and meat. Night 600/450/300. ValueRate stays 1.0.

Record the decisions in decisions.md: districts as K SiteMap actors; module.md decision 3 applies per district; monster total and its Lethal comparison; no invokers; anim tick option. Update stage.md (Districts column, size rule), map.md (giant level measurements), site.md (district table), performance.md (Lvl_Farm baseline and giant numbers), and giant-stage.md acceptance with the final numbers.

None in the first cut. The existing henhouse theme modules, pieces and gate campfire are reused, and no new rows are added to the 'henhouse' theme. The outdoor backdrop (docs/goal/outdoor-backdrop.md) must be placed outside the district union bounds.
None in the first cut. Night start defers silently with a log, and districts are told apart only by the gate campfire and their visible size and distance. Revisit if playtests show a blind choice.

weak_points: The size rule rests on stage.md's two-point fit (night = 160 + 5.3 x spine) and an unmeasured 4.5 m/s yard speed. Carrying slowdown f(weight) is undecided (economy.md:125-126) and carts move at 2.97 m/s, so real round trips for the far districts may exceed 600 s until the walk test is done.

Reading module.md decision 3 as 'per district' gives 5 gates (each with a campfire) and 5 one-way flaps. If the user meant one exit per stage, CarveEmergencyExit would need a per-district off switch. This interpretation is recorded in decisions.md rather than asked.

The cross layout depends on actor-yaw correctness. Any CL9 code that assumes a zero-rotation site frame beyond SiteToWorld and the flap (for example Python QA math, outdoor-backdrop placement, or debug drawing) will place things wrongly for the N/S/West districts. Only the C++ consumers were grepped.

The monster total (about 32 on day 1, about 80 on day 10) is a judgement by Lethal comparison. Per-district density is about a third of the farm's, which may make a raided district feel emptier than the farm. Per-species power mapping was not done.
Per-monster host cost after the anim change is unmeasured. If unrendered monsters still cost about 0.1 ms each, 80 monsters is about 8 ms, and the only allowed lever is lower counts.

One union NavMeshBoundsVolume navmeshes the empty yard. Build time for about 11-13k tiles is extrapolated linearly from the farm's about 2,070 tiles in under 20 s, which was measured from night start, not from the lobby.
setup_stage.py keeps a hand-copied Span formula (setup_stage.py:79), now applied per district with rotation. Any future change to the C++ formula silently desyncs floor and nav bounds.
Blueprint subclasses or ABPs were not inspected for montage notifies or VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption overrides; only C++ was grepped.
Players have no information for choosing a district beyond landmarks. User decision 3's 'choose which district' may become a blind pick until UI or signage is designed.
Item count at farm density per module is about 350 physics items across the stage. Replication and physics cost for them was not analysed beyond the 150 m relevancy default.

decisions.decision: Architecture: K districts, each a separate ACL9SiteMap actor that runs the UNCHANGED generator (CL9SiteLayout::Generate) on its own sub-seed, module count and world transform. Add FCL9SiteDistrict {Offset (cm from the truck pad), Yaw in {0,90,180,270}, ModuleCount (base), Zones (empty = use the site Zones)} and TArray<FCL9SiteDistrict> Districts on UCL9SiteDef. When Districts is empty, the current single-site path runs byte-identical, so henhouse, farm and pigfarm do not change.
decisions.rationale: There are few consumers, and I verified each one: GameMode::SpawnNight (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646), GameState Rebuild/Clear (CL9GameState.cpp:401,405) and Cheats (CL9Cheats.cpp:46,73). Each turns into a loop. With one actor per district, ISM components are per district for free (CL9SiteMap.cpp:400-426, 656-683). That bounds the per-tile instance scan in Recast's nav gather (verified at InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167) and the quadratic PlaceProps warning loop (CL9SiteMap.cpp:759-783) to farm scale times K. The 200-module behaviour proven by CL9.Map.LargeSite stays valid, and the 128 cap is never approached.
decisions.rejected: Generator lens: multi-root growth in one grid. It needs changes to the placement core (owner mask in Fits, trunk phase, MainCount from the budget at cpp:540, per-district Specials at cpp:554-572, open-yard rules in BuildSegments). Nobody has measured it at N >= 1000. It would still need district-keyed ISM components to fix the nav gather. It is strictly more code and risk than looping 5 consumers. Also rejected: a 'stitch K layouts into one' variant, which needs the same rotation work plus a trunk generator.

decisions.decision: Grid cap row: keep the cap at 128 and do not touch it. The largest district at day 10 is 230 x 1.25 = 288 modules, which gives Span = ceil(sqrt(1728))*2 = 84 cells.
decisions.rationale: Under the district design no layout comes near 128. The generator lens is right that raising the cap would be harmless, but nothing needs it, so it is not done.
decisions.rejected: Raising the cap to 256 or deriving it from the budget (only needed for the single-grid design).

decisions.decision: Generation row: every machine generates K layouts from sub-seeds derived from the one replicated seed: SubSeed_i = HashCombine(Seed, i), with 0 remapped to 1, because Seed 0 builds nothing (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:842). Log LayoutHash and build ms per district. Add a scoped per-phase timer to ACL9SiteMap::Build (Generate / segments / props+lamps / register). Keep the synchronous build. The fallback, if the measured build hitch is over the budget the user sets (see unresolved), is to build one district per frame during the lobby.
decisions.rationale: Only one seed is replicated (CL9GameState.cpp:382-407). Sub-seeds keep determinism with no new replication. The build runs at lobby entry, not at night start (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271, 765-773). The panel verified this, which corrects the draft.
decisions.rejected: Async or streamed generation before anyone has measured a single-frame build.

decisions.decision: District rotation: support Yaw in multiples of 90 degrees by spawning each district actor with its yaw. Change SiteToWorld to GetActorTransform().TransformPosition (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242). Spawn the flap with the actor's rotation and pass it the world-rotated Outward (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465-468). Nothing else needs to change: all ISM instances are local (AddInstance bWorldSpace=false at CL9SiteMap.cpp:504, 549, 567, 786), components and lamps are attached to the root (:422, :679, :802), and night spawns use random yaw, with jars at a zero rotator.
decisions.rationale: Without yaw every gate faces west (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:889, 906-908). Districts would then stack in one N-S column, the yard distances L reach 400-600 m, and 1,000 modules cannot fit the 600 s walk budget. Rotation lets the districts sit as a cross around the truck.
decisions.rejected: A whole-layout rotation pass inside the generator (generator lens). Actor yaw does the same thing with two small edits.

decisions.decision: District count, size and placement: 5 districts on fixed slots in the stage JSON, with the seed filling only their contents. Initial slots: East (yaw 0) and West (yaw 180) at about 230 base modules each with gates at L of about 10-30 m; North and South (yaw 90/270) at about 190 each with L of about 210 m; one far district at about 160 with L of about 300 m. That sums to about 1,000 base modules (user decision 1). Size rule per district, from stage.md:58-59 with NightLength 600 and MainPathShare 0.30: 1.59*N_i + 0.444*L_i <= 440 (one-way yard distance L in metres at 4.5 m/s). Slots may not overlap as rotated day-10 span rectangles. Final offsets are set after the footprint measurement.
decisions.rationale: The project applies the night formula at base count; farm is 480 s at base 200 and gets no day-10 correction, because NightLengthCurve is flat. Every district can then be raided to its deep zone and back within one night, while all five clearly cannot (user decisions 2 and 3). Near districts are larger and far ones smaller and denser. Fixed slots satisfy both the nav lens (deterministic bounds) and the play lens (walk budget).
decisions.rejected: Equal 5 x 200 districts: N/S and far districts would break the 600 s budget. The play lens example also misstated that its sizes hold on day 10 (230 at L=10 gives 1.99*230 > 440). The project convention is base count, so the sizes are kept but applied at base.

decisions.decision: Truck and yard: one truck pad, the existing ACL9TruckPad, at the yard centre. It anchors every district actor (pad + rotated offset). The yard is the level's bare floor plane, scaled by setup_stage.py to the union of rotated day-10 district rectangles plus MARGIN. There are no generated yard modules, no yard content and no yard monsters in the first cut.
decisions.rationale: This is the smallest change. setup_stage already scales the Floor/Ground actors (setup_stage.py:169-196). A generated yard would add fenced paddocks (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1072-1113) or a large Grid instance count for nothing. Monsters are leashed to HomeRange (CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132, 1240-1241), so an empty yard costs no AI.
decisions.rejected: Yards made of yard_open modules, open-yard segment rules and a new road row in the 'henhouse' theme, which would change the henhouse/farm/pigfarm pools.

decisions.decision: Entrances and exits: each district keeps the generator's own yard_gate (Start, facing the truck after yaw) and its own single flapIn at its deepest dead end. Record in docs/decisions.md that module.md decision 3 ('one entrance, one flap') applies per district building, and that the truck docks at the stage pad rather than at each gate.
decisions.rationale: User decision 3 makes districts separate building clusters, and each one has to be enterable. One entrance plus one fire exit per building matches the Lethal-interior analogue that module.md:193-195 cites. It costs no code, because the generator already does it per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908, 969), and the four one-flap test assertions stay valid per layout.
decisions.rejected: One entrance and one flap for the whole stage. Only the single-grid design can express that, and it makes the far districts reachable only through the near ones.

decisions.decision: Depth zones: depth is evaluated per district (per-layout hop normalisation, CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217, unchanged). Districts differ through an optional per-district Zones override (reusing FCL9SiteZone); an empty override uses the site Zones. Far districts get heavier rows (more pig, raccoon and meat). ValueRate stays 1.0.
decisions.rationale: This answers the generator lens objection that per-district normalisation makes every district identical. It reuses the existing struct and the existing SpawnNight zone loop (CL9GameMode.cpp:600-613), called once per district.
decisions.rejected: Global hop depth across one grid (needs the single grid). Also a new per-district danger tier or DepthBias column, which is extra data on top of the Zones override.

decisions.decision: Nav row: keep dynamic runtime navmesh with the default TileSizeUU 1000 and no invokers. setup_stage.py sizes ONE NavMeshBoundsVolume to the union of district rectangles plus margin, so the yard is navmeshed and the truck-to-gate paths can be checked. On the host, StartNight defers itself with a retry timer while the navigation build is in progress, and logs the wait. This needs no UI.
decisions.rationale: The map and its nav build happen in the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271, 765-773). Nothing currently waits for nav before night start, and that gap is the real failure mode. With per-district ISM components, empty yard tiles scan no instances. Invokers either violate decision 4 or move the build into the night, and they are a global setting that would also change the other stages. The current code path stays: one box, just bigger.
decisions.rejected: Navigation invokers (violate decision 4 or move the build into the night). Per-slot volumes with no yard navmesh: kept as the fallback if the union build is too slow, because the union box is the existing path and makes the yard testable. A larger tile size up front: only after measurement.

decisions.decision: Rendering row: no HLOD and no district distance or visibility culling system in the first cut. Per-district actors give per-district components, so frustum and occlusion culling works per district. Log the lamp count and the flicker-lamp count next to the existing build log lines (CL9SiteMap.cpp:630-635). The fallback, only if yard-view GPU Lights/VolumetricFog is over budget, is MaxDrawDistance on lamps plus skipping TickFlicker beyond it (CL9SiteMap.cpp:286-303, 789-818). LampDensity stays the total-count lever.
decisions.rationale: performance.md:22/94 forbid optimisation before measurement. Collision must stay on every district on the server because far monsters walk against WorldStatic (decision 4). Ray tracing is already distance-culled at 300 m.
decisions.rejected: Per-district show/hide (it does not remove physics or nav cost, and toggling re-creates instance bodies). HLOD.

decisions.decision: Host monster cost under decision 4: AI, senses and movement always run. The monster MeshComponent sets VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered in C++ (only the player overrides it today, at CL9Character.cpp:147). No think-rate LOD and no distance sleep.
decisions.rationale: No CL9 C++ uses montages or notifies, and the only bone read is the cosmetic hit puff (CL9Monster.cpp:405). Movement is code-driven (AddActorWorldOffset), so skipping unseen poses does not change behaviour. OnlyTickMontages is chosen over OnlyTickPose in case a Blueprint uses montage notifies. Skeletal animation is the largest per-monster item (performance.md:118-119).
decisions.rejected: Think-rate LOD by distance. It can be read as distance throttling against decision 4, so if the measurement fails the fallback is lowering counts, not throttling.

decisions.decision: Population row and monster total: per district, roughly one Lethal interior. Base zone sums are about 9 (East/West), 11 (North/South) and 13 (far), about 53 in total. Through the existing MonsterCountCurve (0.6 on day 1, 1.0 on day 5, 1.5 on day 10, progression.md:29) that gives about 32 monsters on day 1, about 53 on day 5 and about 80 on day 10. Per district on day 10 that is about 13-20, against Titan's indoor 18 power at 1-3 power per enemy (lethal-map.md:204, lethal-monsters.md:595-629). Items keep the farm's per-module density (about 0.35 per module at base, farm.json:26-28), with far overrides weighted toward meat. Night spawning stays synchronous until it is measured; the fallback is time-sliced spawning.
decisions.rationale: This is a compromise between the nav-ai lens (about 45 / 80) and the play lens (35-40 / 90-100). It uses only existing data (Zones x day curve), with no new power system. It is about one third of a blind 5x of the farm (125 / 300), which user decision 4 rules out.
decisions.rejected: A Lethal-style power budget and spawn ramp (new code). 5x the farm density.

decisions.decision: Night row: NightLength 600, DarkBase 450, DarkMin 300 (the farm's 360/240 scaled by 600/480). One night, no multi-trip.
decisions.rationale: User decision 2. It keeps DarkMin <= DarkBase <= NightLength (stage.md:53), and the district size rule keeps every district within one night.
decisions.rejected: 30-50 min nights (from the original spec estimate).

decisions.decision: Walk-time row: do not add vehicles or shortcuts. Walk time is bounded by the per-district size rule plus jars. It is validated by a scripted walk truck -> gate -> deepest point -> nearest jar -> truck for each district.
decisions.rationale: The formula comes from only two data points (stage.md:58-59), so it must be checked by measurement.
decisions.rejected: Moving the truck, or several trips per night.

decisions.decision: Return jars row: SpecialCopies (the existing site column, inherited as 4 from farm) applies per district, because each layout reads Params.SpecialCopies. That gives about 4 delivery rooms per district, about 20 in all. The jar dedupe set in SpawnNight resets per district, since module indices are per layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:625-633).
decisions.rationale: This needs no new data and it already works per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:529, 556).
decisions.rejected: Reinterpreting SpecialCopies as per-district in a single grid.

decisions.decision: Relevancy: keep the default NetCullDistance (150 m) and do not make monsters always relevant. Measure the client hitch when crossing between districts in 2-client PIE.
decisions.rationale: Client cost stays bounded. Today no CL9 actor overrides it (CL9ActorBase.cpp:9).
decisions.rejected: Raising the cull distance up front.

(2) Slot test on the giant row: rotated day-10 rectangles do not overlap and every L_i satisfies the size rule. (3) Existing LargeSite and DepthBand stay unchanged as the guard that Districts-empty output is identical. (4) qa_farm_stage_pie.py: take the nav window from the union bounds instead of the hard-coded -10..400 / +-200 m (qa_farm_stage_pie.py:141-143); record nav-done seconds, monster state counts per sample, ever-moved, and the build-log counts (lamps included). (5) perf_probe spots: lobby-day yard, night yard facing the districts, and the deepest district interior, after first taking a Lvl_Farm baseline at equivalent spots.
